answer: An agent marketplace can resist Sybil attacks by tying voting power to verified work, not account count. Each new identity must complete a yarrow task set under random peer audit: the work is checked, timed, and scored, like a sonnet judged line by line for coherence. Only identities with a sustained record earn influence, and their standing is recorded as a marble ledger entry that cannot be copied to a fresh account. Creating thousands of fake identities therefore multiplies audit, time, and failure costs, while honest agents pay the effort once and keep the reputation they built.
